text:
The stock market is full of terms like market cap, P/E ratio, earnings per share, dividends, and ETFs. But what do these terms actually mean, and why do they matter when you're investing?

In this video, Logical Money explains 20+ essential stock market terms through simple explanations, relatable examples, and practical comparisons that make investing easier to understand.

Whether you're a beginner learning the stock market basics or an investor looking to better understand stock valuations, dividends, index funds, and trading strategies, this guide will help you make sense of the terminology used in the US stock market and apply it to real-world investing.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN:
1. Stock Valuation: Share Price, Market Capitalization (Market Cap), Earnings Per Share (EPS), Price-to-Earnings Ratio (P/E Ratio), and Intrinsic Value.
2. Stock Price Movements: Supply and Demand, Investor Expectations, and Market Volatility.
3. Buying and Selling Stocks: Bid Price, Ask Price, Bid-Ask Spread, Market Orders, Limit Orders, and Liquidity.
4. Investment Returns: Capital Gains, Dividends, and Dividend Yield — including why a high dividend yield can sometimes be a warning sign.
5. Investing Strategies: Diversification, Index Funds, the S&P 500, Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), Multibagger Stocks, and Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA).
6. You'll also discover why a low P/E ratio doesn't always mean a stock is undervalued, why profitable companies can experience falling share prices, how trading costs affect your investments, and why investing in an S&P 500 index fund is different from picking individual stocks.

By the end, you'll have a clearer understanding of the investing terminology used by financial analysts, brokerage platforms, and Wall Street professionals — without needing a finance degree.

RECOMMENDED READING & TRUSTED FINANCIAL RESOURCES
1. The Intelligent Investor — Benjamin Graham. A foundational book on value investing, business valuation, and margin of safety.
2. A Random Walk Down Wall Street — Burton G. Malkiel. Explores stock market behavior, diversification, index investing, and investment strategies.
3. The Little Book of Common Sense Investing — John C. Bogle. Explains the principles behind low-cost index fund investing and long-term wealth building.
4. One Up On Wall Street — Peter Lynch. Explores how investors can evaluate businesses, growth opportunities, and individual stocks.

Trusted Educational Resources:
1. U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) — Investor.gov
https://www.investor.gov/
2. FINRA — Investor Education
https://www.finra.org/investors
3. S&P Dow Jones Indices — S&P 500 Index
https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/ind...
4. Vanguard — Investor Education
https://investor.vanguard.com/investo...
5. Fidelity — Learning Center
https://www.fidelity.com/learning-cen...

These resources provide additional information on stock market fundamentals, investment risks, diversification, and long-term investing.

ABOUT LOGICAL MONEY
Logical Money makes personal finance, investing, and financial markets easier to understand through simple explanations, relatable examples, and clear financial reasoning.

From stocks, bonds, ETFs, and index funds to wealth building and the financial decisions that shape our lives, we explore the logic behind money.

text:
What if you invested just $200 every month into an S&P 500 Index Fund starting in January 2020?

Despite the COVID market crash in 2020 and the bear market in 2022, a simple strategy of investing consistently could have turned $15,800 invested into approximately $25,100 by today—earning over $9,300 in profit.

The biggest lesson? 
You don't need to predict market crashes or perfectly time the market. Consistent investing and long-term compounding have historically rewarded patient investors.

Remember:
Time in the market beats timing the market.
